government_link: No direct state shareholding was identified among holders of 5% or more. The Chairman, HE Sheikh Faisal bin Thani Al Thani, has been Qatar's Minister of Commerce and Industry since Nov 2024, chairs the QFC Authority and QSE, and sits on the QIA board (S9).
group_structure: Lesha Bank LLC (Public) is a QFCRA-authorised Shari'a-compliant investment bank. Its licences cover deposit taking, credit, dealing and arranging, custody, managing investments, advising and operating collective investment funds. Principal subsidiaries at 30 Jun 2026 were mostly investment vehicles: QFB Money Market Fund 1, LB Income Fund, LB Real Estate Equity Fund 1, LB Galaxy PE Fund (new in 2026), QFB Private Equity, LB Education, QFB Hospitality, and US real estate vehicles at 98% held for client products. Two operating subsidiaries were set up in 2025: Lesha Capital Investments (Saudi Arabia, 100%; CMA advisory licence in 2025 and Managing Investments and Operating Funds licence in Feb 2026) and LB Aviation Holdco LLC (Qatar, 100%). Lesha Aviation Capital (LAC) is a separately branded aviation leasing and investment platform launched in 2025, headquartered in Dublin with an office in Doha and a London office opened in Aug 2026. Lesha's GCEO chairs it and the Group CIO is Vice Chairman. The AR 2025 and the Avolon release refer to 'Lesha Aviation Services' as the fleet manager. The legal link between LAC and LB Aviation Holdco is not stated publicly. Bereke Bank (Kazakhstan) was acquired in Oct 2024 and fully syndicated to an investor.

Most income comes from fees and investments: in H1 2026, fee income was QAR 105.3m and dividend income QAR 32.7m.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Lesha Bank is a QFCRA-licensed Shari'a-compliant investment bank whose wealth franchise is its Private Wealth Department (PWD), led by Group Chief Private Wealth Officer Thanwa Al Naimi, who founded the private banking business after joining from QIB in 2014. PWD serves HNW and UHNW individuals, family offices and select institutions. It offers advisory, portfolio management and advisory mandates, structured investments (44 structured investment products serviced in 2025, 19 of them new), public equities and fixed income, and above all access to Lesha's proprietary alternatives deal flow (private equity, real estate, aviation and infrastructure), with periodic investor reporting. In 2025 the RM team grew and gained a dedicated client-services function. Group AUM, labelled off-balance-sheet AUM, was QAR 19.2bn at 30 Jun 2026, up 78% YoY. More than 90% of end-2025 AUM was in aviation, private equity and real estate. Asset management, under Group CIO Glenn Johnstone and Jubin Jose, runs discretionary public equity, fixed income and money market mandates. The H1 2026 strategy plans Qatar and GCC public equity funds, a sukuk fund, an ETF, a Qatar REIT and an evergreen semi-liquid PE fund. Expansion is regional and through partners: Lesha Capital (KSA fund-management licence, Feb 2026), a GIP/BlackRock MoU to co-invest more than US$1bn (Sep 2026), an MoU with Dukhan Bank on investment solutions (Q3 2026) and a DTX Partners VC collaboration (May 2026). No brokerage, digital investing app or client-facing platform was found.

segments.name: Private Wealth (HNW / UHNW)
segments.eligibility: Not published. The AR refers to clients 'who meet our eligibility criteria'.

private_banking.detail: Private Wealth Department: dedicated RMs plus a client-services function. Offers personalised advisory, alternative investments, public equities, fixed income, structured and capital-protected products, term deposits and periodic investor reporting. The website enquiry form lists real estate, health care, education, technology, structured products, term deposit and capital-protected options with USD amounts.

asset_management.detail: In-house asset management covering public equity, fixed income and money market, with growing discretionary mandates for institutional and private clients, plus alternative asset management (PE, real estate, aviation, infrastructure). Fund vehicles include QFB Money Market Fund 1, LB Income Fund, LB Real Estate Equity Fund 1 and LB Galaxy PE Fund (2026). Group AUM was QAR 19.2bn at 30 Jun 2026. Lesha Capital (KSA) holds a CMA Managing Investments and Operating Funds licence (Feb 2026).

brokerage.detail: No brokerage arm or exchange membership was found. The QFCRA licence covers dealing and arranging deals in investments and custody, and the Deputy COO oversees custody services.

digital_investing.detail: No client app or online investing platform found. Digital work in 2025 was internal: a core banking upgrade, a cloud ERP and ISO 20022 messaging.

advisory.detail: Licensed for advising on investments. PWD offers personalised advisory and advisory mandates. Lesha Capital (KSA) has a CMA advisory licence. Investment Banking Advisory serves corporates.

discretionary.detail: The AR 2025 cites 'growth in discretionary mandates' in public equity, fixed income and money market, and 'portfolio management' within Private Wealth. Licensed for managing investments.

funds_platform.detail: Own funds and investment vehicles only. No third-party fund shelf was found. Planned: Qatar and GCC equity funds, a sukuk fund and an ETF (H1 2026 strategy).

structured_products.detail: Operations supported 44 structured investment products in 2025, including 19 new launches. Capital-protected and structured products are offered to private clients, and Treasury covers structured products.

private_markets.detail: This is the core proposition. Clients are offered syndicated private equity, real estate (US, Europe; Qatar REIT planned), aviation (5 B777-300ER, 4 A350-1000; 33 aircraft from Avolon agreed Sep 2026; managed fleet above 75 aircraft) and infrastructure (Edinburgh Airport stake; co-investment with GIP). End-2025 PE AUM was QAR 4.5bn and real estate AUM QAR 4.5bn.

islamic_wealth.detail: Entire bank is Shari'a-compliant. The Shari'a Supervisory Board approves every deal. Products include sukuk (QAR 2.9bn own book), Shari'a-compliant structured products and alternatives.

H1 2026: AUM QAR 19.2bn (+78%), net profit QAR 123.7m (+50.1%), deposits QAR 5.6bn (+78.8%).
DTX Partners collaboration on Shari'a-compliant VC and technology investments.
Lesha Capital (KSA) granted the CMA Managing Investments and Operating Funds licence, in addition to its 2025 advisory licence.
Strategy (H1 2026 presentation): launch Qatar and GCC public equity funds, a sukuk fund and an ETF; raise and list a Qatar REIT; build an evergreen semi-liquid PE fund; launch niche sector funds.

opportunities: Fast-growing HNW/UHNW wealth franchise (AUM +78% YoY to QAR 19.2bn) with no client-facing digital platform or app; client reporting is periodic and RM-led (S4, S7).
Explicit plans to launch public equity funds, a sukuk fund, an ETF and an evergreen semi-liquid PE fund, which need distribution and wrappers (S5).
Building distribution partnerships for its products with other banks (MoU with Dukhan Bank on investment solutions, Q3 2026) and Saudi reach through Lesha Capital (S20, S17).
Large structured-product shelf (44 products, 19 new in 2025) and alternatives syndication suggest a need for scalable portfolio and reporting tools (S7).
barriers: Business model is proprietary alternatives deal flow (aviation, PE, real estate, infrastructure) rather than third-party product shelves; it is itself a product manufacturer (S7, S5).
Fully Shari'a-compliant: the Shari'a Supervisory Board approves every deal (S5).
Small, concentrated client base of HNW/UHNW and institutions, with no published client numbers (S7).
incumbent_vendors: Global Infrastructure Partners (BlackRock) - infrastructure co-investment partner (S12)
Core banking and cloud ERP vendors are not named (S7)

discrepancies.detail: Statements: H1 2026 'TOTAL INCOME' QAR 327,562k and FY2025 QAR 466,621k, both before the quasi-equity share. The H1 release and presentation give 'Total income QAR 239.1m' (statement total income less the quasi-equity share). The FY2025 release gives 'total income of QAR 124 million' (+104%), which matches no statement line.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded the statement 'TOTAL INCOME' lines and noted the release definitions. The FY2025 QAR 124m figure is unresolved, possibly a fee subtotal.

discrepancies.detail: The AR 2025 lists Fulya Plas as Chief Risk Officer. The current website lists Salman Mustafa Siddiqui, who joined in 2026.

The website uses 'Lesha Aviation Capital (LAC)'. The AR 2025 and the Sep 2026 Avolon release refer to 'Lesha Aviation Services' as the business and fleet manager. The financial statements show LB Aviation Holdco LLC (100%).
discrepancies.resolution: All names kept. The legal relationship between the entities is not published.

discrepancies.detail: Spelled Al Zubara / Al Zubarah, Azom / Azum, and Broog / Brouq / Borooq in different documents.

The AR 2025 lists Suhaib Al Mabrouk as Head - Private Equity Investments (and a Mar 2023 release quotes him as Head of Private Equity and Corporate Banking). He does not appear on the Management Team page checked 12 Oct 2026, which names no private equity head.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded as 'Conflicting sources'; no departure or successor announcement found.

discrepancies.detail: CG Report 2025 prints 'Appointed on 11 July 2024'. Gulf Times reported the appointment on 11 Jul 2023 ('officially assumed his responsibilities in July'), and Forbes ME (Jul 2026) says he assumed the position in 2023.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded Jul 2023; the CG Report year treated as a slip (the day and month match the 2023 announcement).

discrepancies.detail: AR 2025 and the CG Report organisation chart name Khalid Al Arid as Head - IT; the website (Oct 2026) lists Benjamin Gaskin as Head of Technology.
discrepancies.resolution: Gaskin recorded as current (official page); appointment date unknown.

discrepancies.detail: Website: oversees private equity, real estate investments and public equities. CG Report 2025: oversees private equity, real estate investment and wealth management businesses.
discrepancies.resolution: Both wordings recorded; no reporting line inferred.

discrepancies.detail: The website prefixes Group to the CEO, CIO, CPWO, CFO, CRO, CLO and DCOO titles; the AR 2025 and CG Report 2025 omit it.

open_items: Q3 2026 (30 Sep 2026) results not yet on QSE: the API returned 404 for QFBQ 2026-09-30 on 12 Oct 2026.
The Dukhan Bank MoU on investment solutions was found only in Dukhan's 9M 2026 release, not on Lesha's news pages. Date and terms are unknown.
The Private Wealth client count, minimum investment and Private Wealth-specific AUM are not published.
Lesha Aviation Capital / Lesha Aviation Services executives and legal ownership were not verified (out of scope, as in the original).
The 17 Sep 2026 QSE major-shareholder snapshot cited in the original was not re-checked; 31 Dec 2025 data was used.
Employee headcount was not extracted from the 61 MB annual report (keyword search only).

LinkedIn (X23): the official pages link only the company LinkedIn page and the search tool declines name-based look-ups of individuals, so no new personal URLs could be sought; the original verified URLs for Thanwa Al Naimi and Glenn Johnstone are retained without re-opening; decision-makers without a URL are marked 'Not verified', others 'Not checked'.

People pass X23: appointment years for Jose (2024, website), Bernassau, Gaskin and Al Mabrouk are not in the CG Report 2025, which profiles only part of the management team. The Chairman's first appointment date in 2022 was not found in a dated document (inferred from the Mar 2023 AGM release and the CG Report's 2022 board election).

Not added (X23): Group Chief Legal Officer and Board Secretary Rita El Helou (appointed 2021), Head of Operations Prem Anandh Kasilingam, Head of Middle Office Mohamed Thahir, Head of Corporate Services Ahmed Abou Elela (appointed 2020), Director of Marketing Maryam Al Malki (2025) and Director of Internal Audit Shahzad Hussain (2021), all on the official page and/or in the CG Report 2025; the nine-member board (elected 24 Feb 2025 for three years) and the three-member Shari'a Supervisory Board (Sheikh Dr Walid Bin Hadi, Chairman) are not profiled beyond the Chairman.
